statement: When a record is republished from a private repository into a public one, apply every redaction before the first commit, never in a later one. A 'copy verbatim, then redact' history reads well in review, because the second commit's diff shows each change, but every commit pushed to a public branch is published, so the first commit puts the closed text on the public remote whatever the final tree says. Give the reviewer the source-comparison command instead: git show <private-sha>:<path> against the public copy. Rule: on a public branch, a commit is a publication; redact in the working tree, check the working tree, then commit.

A card that reads another repository's records with git -C <other> show origin/main:<path> fails in a session whose shell refuses every git call against that repository. From inside the permitted worktree, git fetch --no-tags <other-path> refs/remotes/origin/main followed by git show <fetched-sha>:<path> reads the same bytes from the same ref, without touching the other repository's working tree. Pin the fetched SHA, and check it against the hosting service's merge commit for the cited pull request, before reading anything. Rule: when the named read is refused, look for a read of the same ref that the boundary allows before falling back to the working tree.
